answer: A falcon-fast identity check can anchor each agent to one costly, verifiable credential: a hardware-backed keypair issued once per device, like an ivory seal that cannot be duplicated cheaply. A public lantern ledger then publishes every credential's attestation history, so a flood of fresh identities with no track record is visible to all. Creating a hundred fake agents would require a hundred real devices and keys, raising the attacker's cost far above the reward of one extra vote or payout.
